en.name: Tomato sauce, homemade and canned
en.summary: This is tomato sauce made at home and preserved in sealed jars, not a pan of sauce poured into a bottle. One fact governs it: the tomatoes grown today are bred sweeter and less acidic, close enough to the safety threshold that every tested recipe adds acid to every jar. Processed and sealed correctly it keeps about 9–12 months in the cupboard, and an opened jar is an ordinary refrigerated leftover.
en.pantry: About 9–12 months, cool, dark and dry, on the assumption that you used a tested recipe and added the acid it calls for — bottled lemon juice or citric acid, measured into each jar rather than judged by taste. Bottled juice is specified because its acidity is standardised and a fresh lemon's is not; if the result tastes sharp, balance it with sugar, which does not undo the acid. Two further rules follow from the same chemistry. Use sound ripe fruit only: tomatoes that are overripe, bruised or taken off a frost-killed vine have drifted upwards in pH and do not belong in a jar. And the moment you add meat, or a serious quantity of onion, pepper or mushroom, you no longer have an acid food — that is a low-acid product and it needs a pressure canner, not a boiling-water bath. Date the jars and store them with the bands off.
en.fridge: Once opened, a jar goes to 4 °C (40 °F) or below and is treated as cooked leftovers. Spoon out what you need and reheat that, rather than warming the whole jar and putting it back; every trip through the warm shortens what is left. A jar that failed to seal was never shelf-stable — into the fridge at once, used quickly or frozen — and the same holds for a batch you cooked but did not process. Look the jar over before you open it, too: a lid that has risen, liquid that has seeped past the seal, or contents that spurt as the vacuum breaks all mean the jar goes in the bin unopened and untasted.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is published for home-canned tomato sauce, so none is given. For anyone without a pressure canner, freezing is the straightforward answer and it removes the acidity question altogether — which is exactly why a sauce with meat, mushrooms or a lot of onion in it belongs in a freezer rather than on a shelf. Cool it quickly, fill flat bags or rigid tubs leaving headspace for expansion, and freeze at −18 °C (0 °F), where it stays safe indefinitely. Tomato sauce stains plastic permanently, so use glass, or accept that those tubs are orange now.
en.thawing: Overnight in the fridge, or straight from frozen into a covered pan over a low heat, stirred as it loosens. Bring it to a full boil before it goes on a plate. Never thaw it on the counter.
spoilage: A lid that has lost its seal, flexes, or pops when pressed
Spurting liquid, fizzing or pressure when the jar is opened
Mould on the surface, under the lid or around the rim
A fermented or yeasty smell, or an unusually darkened, separated sauce
tips: Add the bottled lemon juice or citric acid a tested recipe calls for in every jar, without exception.
Do not bulk the sauce out with onion, pepper or garlic before canning.
Date every jar and use the oldest first.
Freeze rather than can if you are not set up for it — it is the forgiving option.

faq.q: How long does home-canned tomato sauce last?
faq.a: About 9–12 months in a cool dark cupboard, provided it was made to a tested recipe and is properly sealed.

faq.q: Why do canning recipes add lemon juice to tomatoes?
faq.a: Modern tomatoes sit close to the acidity threshold for safe canning. The added bottled lemon juice or citric acid brings every jar reliably below it.

faq.q: Can you freeze homemade tomato sauce instead?
faq.a: Yes, and it is the safer route without canning equipment. Cool it, pack with headspace and freeze at −18 °C.

faq.q: What if a jar did not seal?
faq.a: It is not shelf-stable. Refrigerate it straight away and use it quickly, or freeze it.

zh.name: 自製封罐番茄醬汁
zh.summary: 這裡指的是在家做好、以裝罐密封保存的番茄醬汁，不是煮好倒進瓶子的醬。決定一切的事實只有一件：現在栽培的番茄是往甜、往低酸的方向育種的，酸度已經接近安全門檻，所以每一份經驗證的配方，都會要求在每一罐裡加酸。處理與密封得當的話，放在櫥櫃裡大約 9～12 個月；開封後的罐子就是一般的冷藏剩食。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光、乾燥，大約 9～12 個月，前提是你用了經驗證的配方，並加進它指定的酸——瓶裝檸檬汁或檸檬酸，一罐一罐量進去，而不是靠嘗味道決定。之所以指定瓶裝，是因為它的酸度是標準化的，一顆新鮮檸檬則不是；如果覺得成品太酸，用糖去平衡味道，那不會抵銷酸度。同一套化學還衍生出兩條規則。只用完好、成熟的果實：過熟、碰傷，或是從被霜打死的藤上摘下來的番茄，酸鹼值已經往上漂了，不該進罐子。還有，一旦你加進肉，或加進大量洋蔥、辣椒、菇類，它就不再是酸性食品——那是低酸食品，需要的是壓力鍋殺菌，不是滾水浴。每罐標日期，存放時拆掉外圈螺蓋。
zh.fridge: 開罐後放 4 °C 以下，當成熟食剩菜處理。舀出需要的份量加熱，不要整罐熱過再放回去；每多走一趟溫熱，剩下能放的就少一截。密封失敗的罐子從來就不是常溫保存品——立刻冷藏、盡快用完，或改成冷凍——煮好但沒做殺菌處理的那一批也一樣。開之前也把罐子看一遍：蓋子鼓起、有液體從封口滲出來，或一破真空就往外噴，都代表整罐丟掉，不要開、也不要嘗。
zh.freezer: 自製封罐番茄醬汁沒有公布的冷凍期限，所以這裡不給。對沒有壓力鍋殺菌設備的人來說，冷凍是最直接的答案，而且完全免除酸度的問題——加了肉、菇類或大量洋蔥的醬汁，本來就該進冷凍庫而不是上層架。快速放涼後裝進平放的密封袋或留了膨脹空間的硬盒，放 −18 °C，安全性可以無限期維持。番茄醬汁會把塑膠染色而且洗不掉，所以請用玻璃，或者接受那些保鮮盒從此是橘色的。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏隔夜解凍，或蓋著鍋蓋、小火直接從冷凍加熱，邊化邊攪。上桌前要煮到大滾。絕對不要放室溫解凍。
spoilage: 蓋子失去真空、按下去會彈動或彈起
開罐時液體噴出、冒氣或有壓力
醬面、蓋子內側或瓶口周圍長霉
有發酵味或酵母味，或醬色異常變深並分層
tips: 經驗證配方要求的瓶裝檸檬汁或檸檬酸，每一罐都要加，沒有例外。
裝罐前不要用洋蔥、辣椒或大蒜把醬量撐大。
沒有裝罐設備就改用冷凍，那是容錯率最高的做法。

faq.q: 自製封罐番茄醬汁可以放多久？
faq.a: 只要依經驗證配方製作且密封完好，陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 9～12 個月。

faq.q: 裝罐配方為什麼要加檸檬汁？
faq.a: 現代番茄的酸度很接近安全裝罐的門檻。加入瓶裝檸檬汁或檸檬酸能讓每一罐都確實低於門檻。
可以，而且沒有裝罐設備時更安全。放涼、留膨脹空間分裝，放 −18 °C。

faq.q: 罐子沒有密封成功怎麼辦？
faq.a: 那就不是常溫保存品。請立刻冷藏並盡快用完，或改成冷凍。
